RESULT: F1 HIGH (tested, stdlib): scene crashes on one malformed-but-validated JSON packet. measurement_contract.validate() returns early for detection_valid=false without checking source_K, and decode() only rejects NaN/Infinity literals, so 1e999 parses to inf. scene_state.py:88 then runs json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) on K and raises ValueError. scene_node.py:177 catches only (ContractError, KeyError, TypeError, OverflowError), so the exception leaves the main loop and scene exits. Same class: scene_state.py:167 dict(packet['live_stage_ms']) is never validated; ['abc'] raises ValueError (reproduced) and also escapes. split_supervisor then tears down both nodes. Fix: catch Exception per packet and fail closed, and validate/strip source_K, live_stage_ms and other optional fields in validate() for both valid and invalid packets.

F2 HIGH (tested contract path; node path static): perception can be killed by a single bad camera frame. perception_node.py:185-187 publishes the unqualified-image record with K=list(info.k). image_qualified() rejects non-finite K, but camera_measurement()->encode() then raises ContractError (reproduced with NaN K), and neither publish() at perception_node.py:102 nor the main-loop call sites catch it. The same uncaught path applies to any pipeline record with NaN/inf or oversize values from the detector (the loop at ~138-153). One bad CameraInfo or detector value stops the camera node and the supervisor then stops the scene node. Fix: sanitize K (use null) on the unqualified path, and catch ContractError at publish to emit a bare detection_valid=false measurement or count a reject.

F3 MEDIUM (static, plausible; intended old-policy not verified): settle_s is not applied to image time. stable_observation.py:127-128 FeedbackWindow.at() checks (self.last-self.start)>=settle_s using the latest feedback time, and only requires image_t>=self.start. An image taken at start+0.1s is accepted as soon as feedback matures, e.g. when processed at start+0.6s (still within the 0.5s image age), so frames from the settling window can enter snapshots with a valid base transform. Suggested check: (image_t-self.start)>=settle_s.

F4 MEDIUM (static): ROI hint can pin to stale geometry. scene_state.py:161-163 only updates self.roi when the current frame has usable complete targets and never clears it otherwise. hint() (scene_state.py:~178) sends the old roi_xyxy with fresh based_on_stamp_ns/issued_ns, so the hint looks current although the ROI is from older frames. Perception forces full frame only every 18th inference (perception_node.py:~199). If pieces move or leave the ROI, up to 17 frames are inferred in a crop that cannot see them, and scene's _scene_matches count comparison can mismatch/invalidate snapshots. Fix: carry the ROI source stamp and expire it, or clear self.roi when a frame has no usable targets.

F5 LOW (static): any rejected packet (duplicate, reordered, expired, malformed) goes through reject_packet (scene_state.py:64-69). It sets observation.pending=True and state='pending_confirmation', and it publishes an expired/revoked copy of last_record on /pose/xiangqi/detections. One late or duplicate BEST_EFFORT packet, or one packet from a second publisher on the topic, therefore revokes current coordinates and snapshot eligibility until the next good fresh frame. It also overwrites state 'consumed'/'locked'. Consider counting stale/duplicate rejects without revoking current state, and only revoking on genuinely invalid or new-epoch packets. Related: stable_observation.py:334 can divide by zero when all confidences are 0, since contract allows confidence==0 and ZeroDivisionError is not caught at scene_node.py:177.
EVIDENCE: Stdlib script imported measurement_contract: decode('..."source_K":1e999...') -> inf; validate() returned the packet; json.dumps(allow_nan=False) -> ValueError; dict(['abc']) -> ValueError; camera_measurement with NaN K -> ContractError.

Paths read: REVIEW_REQUIREMENTS.txt, measurement_contract.py, scene_state.py, scene_node.py, perception_node.py, split_supervisor.py, stable_observation.py, qualification.py, base_geometry.py. Launchers, piece_tracker.py, shared_pipeline.py and tests were not read.

Positive checks, no finding: acquisition stamp_ns is preserved end to end and perception_publish_ns is kept separate; SequenceGuard rejects duplicate/reordered/retired epochs and clears frame keys on epoch change; scene _retire clears tracker, snapshot sampling and ROI on epoch change; ROI hint requires source epoch, a published (sequence, stamp), finite integer bounds and <=0.3s freshness, with perception falling back to full frame; snapshot uniqueness uses rgbd_frame_key; collecting requires a full-frame inference ROI; scene queues are bounded (deque maxlen 4/32/512, byte cap 1 MiB).
VALIDATION: Only stdlib experiments on measurement_contract.py. numpy, ROS and scipy are not installed, so scene_state, stable_observation, perception_node and scene_node were reviewed statically and not executed. No tests were run. No source, Git or network changes.
RISKS: F1/F2 are availability/fail-closed issues; there is no evidence of unsafe qualification. All motion_ready/grasp_ready paths stay False.
F3 intent depends on the old Experiment's settle semantics, which were not checked. F4 impact depends on the 18-frame full-frame cadence and PieceTracker behavior.
Other unreviewed unhandled exception sources in scene process() (tracker.update, observe) could produce the same crash class as F1.

Review limitation: Not reviewed: piece_tracker.py, shared_pipeline.py, the launchers and tests. The PieceTracker.update exception surface and the pipeline record schema (e.g. whether image_size is always present on detection_valid=false records) are unverified.
